body.statement: On the strictly positive outcome chart, for fixed \((r,w,\pi)\), \(m_1-m_0\) is strictly increasing in \(\theta\), and \(q-r=(\pi-w)(m_1-m_0)\).  Hence the extrema over \(\theta\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\) occur at \(\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\): if \(\pi-w\geq0\), the lower and upper choices are \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\) and \(\Gamma_a\), while the choices reverse if \(\pi-w\leq0\).
body.justification: The lemma reduces a continuum of outcome-association choices to two analytic sign branches.
body.gap: VanderWeele--Arah expose the same bias product, but do not prove endpoint reduction under two-sided odds budgets and a shared posterior pair.
body.consumer: Applied sensitivity software needs only evaluate the two calibrated outcome-odds endpoints in each branch.
